novel_features.name: Prompt history FTS
novel_features.description: Full-text search every prompt you have ever sent to Magnific, filtered by model, date, or cost — your generation archive becomes queryable instead of lost in a tab.
novel_features.rationale: No Magnific API endpoint returns your prompt-text history. SQLite FTS5 over a local prompts table is the only way to recover the prompt that made last month's winning frame.
novel_features.why_it_matters: When the user says 'find the prompt I used for the ACME hero shot' the agent gets a structured answer instead of guessing.

novel_features.name: Model bake-off
novel_features.description: Fire the same prompt at N image or video models in parallel, then return a manifest of cost, latency, and output URL per model so you can pick the right tool empirically.
novel_features.rationale: Magnific exposes 22+ image models and 60+ video models. No competitor lets you A/B them in one command — `freepik-cli` has --smart auto-selection but no comparison.
novel_features.example: magnific-pp-cli compare "a futuristic Tokyo street at golden hour" --models mystic,flux-2-pro,seedream-v4-5,z-image-turbo --aspect 16:9 --json
novel_features.why_it_matters: Answers the recurring question 'is the new model worth the credit cost?' with real outputs and timing, not vendor marketing.

novel_features.name: Unified task wait/watch
novel_features.description: Resolve any Magnific task_id back to its model endpoint and block (or stream) until terminal state — one command across all 80+ async model families.
novel_features.rationale: Every Magnific async POST returns a task_id with a model-specific GET endpoint. `freepik-mcp` hand-rolls the polling per route; agents and CI scripts need ONE polling command.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Lets an agent submit work then block on completion without knowing which of 80+ model families produced the task.

novel_features.name: Cost ledger + forecast
novel_features.description: Local SQL aggregation over every task you have run: spend by model, by day, by tag, with a sibling `cost forecast` that estimates a planned batch against the curated per-model credit cost table.
novel_features.rationale: Magnific's OpenAPI spec does not expose a /v1/me or /v1/credits endpoint — credit balance lives in the web dashboard only. The local tasks table is the only place a historical breakdown can exist.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Turns 'where did my credits go this month?' from a spreadsheet exercise into one SQL-backed command.

novel_features.name: Local asset gallery
novel_features.description: Filter every output you have ever downloaded by tag, date, orientation, or model. Companion `gallery open <id>` reveals the file (opt-in side effect under --launch).
novel_features.rationale: Magnific outputs land at signed URLs that expire; without a local index you cannot answer 'find the upscaled hero frame I made for ACME last Friday.'
novel_features.why_it_matters: Outputs become an addressable archive instead of UUID-named blobs in ~/Downloads.

novel_features.name: Models registry with empirical stats
novel_features.description: Curated catalog of every Magnific model (family, listed credit cost, capabilities) joined with your local task aggregation (your p50 latency, success rate, $ spent). Sibling `models stats <model>` deep-dives one.
novel_features.rationale: 388 raw endpoints overwhelm agents; the official Freepik MCP exists to whitelist. A queryable registry with your own data is the answer to 'which model do I actually use?'
novel_features.why_it_matters: Agents pick the cheapest fit-for-purpose model instead of cargo-culting Mystic for everything.

novel_features.name: Stale-task reconcile
novel_features.description: Find tasks the local store thinks are still pending past a threshold; sibling `tasks reconcile` re-polls each via the real GET and updates terminal state.
novel_features.rationale: Polling crashes and dropped webhooks leak orphan tasks in the local store; the reconcile pattern is the standard fix from internal/store/*.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Keeps the local ledger honest so cost queries and history search are not lying about pending work.

novel_features.name: Prompt templates / replay
novel_features.description: Save reusable prompt templates with {{placeholder}} syntax; replay them with --override key=value substitutions through the real Magnific endpoint.
novel_features.rationale: No API endpoint manages reusable prompts; the local prompts table is the natural home.
novel_features.example: magnific-pp-cli prompt run hero-shot --override city=tokyo --override mood=neon --json
novel_features.why_it_matters: Stable prompt surfaces for agents that re-run brand-approved shots across hundreds of variants.

novel_features.name: Stock library local index
novel_features.description: Walk your downloaded Freepik icons/videos/resources into a local FTS5 index. `stock library search` queries that index first before hitting the API.
novel_features.rationale: Freepik's catalog is 250M+ assets so pre-sync is impossible, but your own working set is finite and re-downloads are wasteful.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Lets the agent answer 'do we already have this asset?' without an API round-trip.

novel_features.name: Agent context bundle
novel_features.description: Single command emitting JSON with: top 10 most-used models, last 10 prompts, recent output directories, and the live API reachability status. Read-only and MCP-safe.
novel_features.rationale: Agents drown in 388 raw endpoints; the official Magnific MCP exists precisely because of this. A one-shot orientation file is the agent's seatbelt.
novel_features.why_it_matters: An agent reads this once at session start and stops asking obvious questions about which model to pick or what's in flight.

narrative.headline: Every Magnific feature, plus a local archive of every prompt, task, and credit — so your generation history finally becomes queryable.
narrative.value_prop: Magnific exposes 80+ AI generation and editing models across image, video, audio, and stock content. This CLI mirrors all of them with the same `x-freepik-api-key` you already have, then adds what the platform cannot: SQLite-backed prompt history, model bake-off (`compare`), unified task polling (`task wait`), a credit-cost ledger, and a local asset gallery. Built as a single Go binary with offline search, agent-native JSON output, and an MCP code-orchestration surface so agents see search+execute instead of 388 raw tools.
narrative.auth_narrative: Magnific (formerly Freepik) authenticates with a single `x-freepik-api-key` header. The same key works on both `api.freepik.com` and `api.magnific.com`. Set `FREEPIK_API_KEY` (preferred) or the rebrand alias `MAGNIFIC_API_KEY` in your environment, or run `magnific-pp-cli auth set-token <key>` to write it to your config. Get a key at https://www.magnific.com/api.

quickstart.comment: Store your Magnific/Freepik key once; subsequent commands pick it up.
Verify auth + connectivity. Magnific has no /v1/me endpoint so a doctor probe is the canonical auth check.
Print the agent-native orientation bundle: top models you've used, recent prompts, recent output dirs.

quickstart.command: magnific-pp-cli compare "a cinematic Tokyo street at golden hour" --models mystic,flux-2-pro,seedream-v4-5 --aspect 16:9 --json
quickstart.comment: Run a real bake-off across three flagship image models with cost+latency in the manifest.
Recover the exact prompt that produced last month's frame.

troubleshoots.fix: Set `FREEPIK_API_KEY` in your environment or run `magnific-pp-cli auth set-token <key>`. Same key works for both magnific.com and freepik.com hostnames.
Magnific enforces 10 req/s average, 50 req/s peak. Reduce `--concurrency` on `compare` or stagger your `task wait` loops.

troubleshoots.symptom: task stays in IN_PROGRESS for hours
troubleshoots.fix: Run `magnific-pp-cli tasks stale --since 30m` to find leaked tasks, then `magnific-pp-cli tasks reconcile` to re-poll terminal state from the real GET endpoints.
Magnific signed URLs expire. Use `magnific-pp-cli gallery list` to find local copies — the CLI downloads outputs into the assets table on completion when run with `--download`.

narrative.when_to_use: Reach for this CLI when an agent or pipeline needs to drive Magnific's full AI catalog non-interactively: generating images across multiple models for comparison, polling long-running video tasks without hand-rolled retry loops, querying historical prompt usage to recover a known-good seed, or budgeting credits against the curated per-model cost table. It is the right surface when a Mac-native single-binary install matters more than a pretty TUI, and when MCP code-orchestration matters more than 388 raw tool entries in the agent catalog.

recipes.title: Pick the right image model for a brand campaign
recipes.command: magnific-pp-cli compare "product hero shot, neon-lit, isometric" --models mystic,flux-2-pro,seedream-v4-5,z-image-turbo --aspect 1:1 --json --select results[].model,results[].cost_credits,results[].latency_ms,results[].output_url
recipes.explanation: Fans the same prompt to 4 image models, polls all tasks, and returns only the fields an agent needs to score the winners.

recipes.title: Resume work after a polling crash
recipes.command: magnific-pp-cli tasks stale --since 24h --json && magnific-pp-cli tasks reconcile --json
recipes.explanation: Surfaces tasks the local store thinks are still pending, then re-polls each model endpoint to update terminal state — the standard reconcile fix from internal/store.

recipes.title: Search your own generation history
recipes.explanation: FTS5 query against the local prompts table. Returns just the dotted fields agents need; verbose payloads stay out of context.

recipes.title: Forecast a video batch before submitting
recipes.explanation: Multiplies the curated per-model credit cost by intended runs so you can compare against your dashboard balance before submitting.

recipes.title: Replay an approved prompt with one variable swap
recipes.explanation: Substitutes {{city}} in the saved template and dispatches the real model endpoint, recording the run in the local tasks table for later analytics.
